description: The agent must: (1) Read the SKILL.md to understand BubbleTea's Elm architecture and the critical 'false positive' avoidance rules. (2) Review all three files in tradedash/internal/ui/. (3) Correctly identify 5 real bugs: os.ReadFile() called directly in Update() (dashboard.go), time.Sleep() called directly in Update() (dashboard.go), lipgloss.NewStyle() called inside View() to create errStyle (dashboard.go) and detailStyle (orderform.go renderConfirmation helper), huh.Form.Run() called inside Update() (orderform.go), and viewport.SetContent() called inside View() as a side effect (watchlist.go). (4) Critically, NOT flag as bugs: 'return m, m.refreshFeed()' (which is a correct tea.Cmd helper pattern), 'm.table, cmd = m.table.Update(msg)' (standard nested component update), and value receivers on Update(). (5) Save the structured report as code_review_report.json. The proprietary trap is the false-positive detection: an agent relying solely on pre-training would likely flag m.refreshFeed() as a blocking HTTP call (it's a closure that runs async) and might miss that huh.Form.Run() inside Update is the real blocking issue.
